subfield: Astrophysics / radio transients and neutron stars
motivation: In 2007 Lorimer, Bailes and McLaughlin found a single, highly dispersed millisecond radio burst in archival Parkes pulsar-survey data. Its dispersion measure placed it far outside our Galaxy. This 'Lorimer burst' revealed a new class of astrophysical phenomenon: fast radio bursts. Surveys have since detected thousands of them. FRBs have been localized to host galaxies, and the magnetar SGR 1935+2154 has been identified as a Galactic source, showing that at least some FRBs come from highly magnetized neutron stars. Because FRB dispersion counts every ionized baryon along the line of sight, FRBs have become a new cosmological tool. They have been used to locate the 'missing' baryons in the intergalactic medium, to measure intergalactic magnetic fields and to constrain the Hubble constant. Their discovery rested on careful single-pulse searching methods that these nominees pioneered. It opened a new area of the transient universe and a new probe of fundamental physics.
